title: Bhairavānukaraṇastotra — Hymn of Becoming like Bhairava
author: Kṣemarāja
text:
The Bhairavānukaraṇastotra is a five-song hymn by Kṣemarāja (c. tenth–eleventh century), the great systematizer of the recognition school and commentator on Utpaladeva. The title states its aim: the imitation of Bhairava — not as metaphor but as actual conformity of the devotee to the Lord's condition. Its stanzas move through salutation and shelter, forbid wandering after lesser supports, and set grace itself as the force that conquers; the divine spread of the Self is invoked as already operative.

Its juice: to become like Bhairava is to cease rehearsing separation. Kṣemarāja's craft is to make each verse enact what it asserts — the hymn shelters rather than describes, and grace, not effort, is given the victory.
